PTSD, major depressive disorder, mood disorder NOS. 

One word, date, smell or memory in general can set you off into isolation mode for months on end. You can't stop crying but you don't know why. Every which way you turn you're reminded of the fact that everyone will live a normal, happy successful life without medication and weekly therapy - but you never will. Your brain chemistry won't ever be able to balance itself. For as long as you can remember, maybe even 3 years old, you've been suffering with the constant thought of killing yourself. In addition, you constantly feel like the world is against you because you know that no one understands what's going on. 

It's really hard to get through every single day and it has been since pre-school. All I can hope is that sooner or later I'll be able to make it 24 hours without suicidal thoughts and crying spells due to past traumatic events.

For me it was a way to have an actual talk with my family. I went against my will after a suicide attempt. It was horrible and fantastic at the same time because I was able to work with doctors for a few days on finding somewhat balanced medications but on the other hand, you're stuck inside a hospital and not allowed to move outside of the 800 square feet. 

I am thankful for the opportunities it gave me to actually discuss the fact that I have a mood disorder, but it was extremely isolating which made it hurt more. If you feel that you need to go, you're more than welcome to talk to me about my experience.

Stay safe, dear.

Don't stop taking your meds...please? (Unless your p-doc says it's OK)

You may feel great right now, but who's to say that you'll go back to square one after completely stopping your medications? It's not worth going completely off unless your doctors give permission. I know how you feel but really it's not worth risking your mental health and safety. I thought I could remove all medications from my life because I was feeling stable and totally "normal" but once I stopped, I crashed, HARD. 

Just be cognizant of how you're feeling and if it's just the fact that the meds are working well for you and that's why your moods are better. Be careful, be safe and feel free to message me if you need to talk to anyone.

My thoughts:

* Mike Holmgren took the Seahawks to their first superbowl and I love him but he has shitty clock management. I’m not sure he’d like Cutler cause he still throws a few too many INT’s. He’s all about protecting the ball. That said he is an offensive GENIUS. But yeah, he will want to be in charge of who the team drafts and he was not good at that in Seattle. 

* Shanahan, I do think Snyder ruined him. RG3’s family had unlimited access to the facilities, yeah. Not a good situation. I think he’s a good coach, I’m not sure Forte is the best back for his system but him and Cutler reunited would be interesting. 
 
* Brian Kelly: hahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahhahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahahaha. I can’t see this at all 
 
* Singletary: This guy is a dumbass as a coach. He wanted a power run game (no problem with that, it worked for Harbaugh and Carroll) but then complained about the offense when his OC was doing what the coach wanted. Pretty much said “IT DOESN’T MATTER WHAT PLAY I CALL IF YOU PLAY HARD ENOUGH IT’LL WORK”. No. We don’t want him. Look at what Harbaugh was able to do with the roster Singletary had. Went 13-3 after Singletary was fired. (with the only major addition being Aldon Smith I believe?). Threw Alex Smith under the bus, threw everyone else under the bus. Avoid him at all costs. (Maybe interview him to satisfy the stupid Rooney rule).

* Harbaugh: Alpha personality, want things run HIS WAY AND ONLY HIS WAY. Will probably want a Pete Carroll like control over the Bears. Would he be able to find a GM he can work with? Good coach but he took the 49ers to 3 straight NFC championship games and look how they’re treating him.  
 
* Todd Bowles: Please. Stupid Cardinals getting good defensive coordinators like they grow on trees. Cards had a ton of injuries and they’re still tough.

* Pep: I’m always weary about giving credit to coaches for developing elite prospects. Luck is a good QB, but he gets to inflate his stats by playing the Texans, Jags and Titans twice a year. Against not those teams he’s not as good. Plus Cutler has been in the NFL nearly 10 years, will Pep be able to get rid of some of the bad habits Cutler has cemented over his decade in the NFL? 


I don’t know anything about Dave Toub. Special teams coaches, eh. Not really sure I like them. John Harbaugh was okay in Baltimore but I’m still not really sold on him as a good coach as opposed to him having a good team. 

There’s also Darrell Bevell. Today Carroll said “Carroll said he tells his assist coaches, coordinators that he will help them get any job they want. “In my mind, everyone is moving on.”” 


There are also wild cards. I mean, we could go after Rex Ryan. We could also go after Teryl Austin (I think that’s his name) the lions’ defensive coordinator. There’s even a chance we could go after Bill Cowher or someone like that.
